library(repli)

# Introduction

Missing values are common in mass spectrometry-based proteomics data and can complicate downstream statistical analysis. Imputation can be used to retain proteins with incomplete measurements, providing valuable biological insights that might otherwise be missed.

`repli` implements replicate-based imputation for Missing At Random (MAR) data, where values are present for some but not all replicates of an experimental condition. The method uses measurements from other replicates of the same protein-condition combination to determine the mean of the imputation distribution. A global standard deviation is derived from all protein-condition pairs in the dataset and used as the standard deviation of the imputation distribution.

The package provides two workflows:

- a data-frame workflow for users working with standard R data frames;
- a `SummarizedExperiment` workflow for users working with proteomics analysis packages such as `DEP`.

# Input data

`repli` expects samples to follow a condition-replicate naming convention, with an underscore or period as separator:

```text
condition_replicate
```

For example:

```text
control_1
control_2
control_3
treatment_1
treatment_2
treatment_3
```

The data should contain proteins in rows and samples in columns.

# Data-frame workflow

## Preparing the data

First, prepare the data using `prepare_imputation_data()`.

```{r preparing data}
data(example_dataset)
prepared <- prepare_imputation_data(example_dataset)
```

The resulting object contains the prepared data as well as the information required for imputation.

```{r inspect prepared data}
names(prepared)
```

Protein-condition combinations are classified as:

- `Valid`: no missing values;
- `MAR`: some missing values;
- `MNAR`: all missing values.

## Performing replicate-based imputation

The prepared data can be passed to `impute_replicate()`:

```{r imputing data}
set.seed(123)

imputed <- impute_replicate(prepared)
```

The random seed can be set to make the stochastic imputation reproducible.

# SummarizedExperiment workflow

For users working with `SummarizedExperiment` objects, `impute_replicate_se()` combines preparation, imputation, and reconstruction into a single function.

```{r imputing SummarizedExperiment object}
data(example_se)

set.seed(123)

imputed_se <- impute_replicate_se(
  example_se,
  p = 0.05
)
```

The returned object is a `SummarizedExperiment` with the imputed assay.

```{r inspect SE object}
class(imputed_se)
```

This workflow is intended to integrate directly with downstream proteomics workflows based on `DEP`.

# Mixed MAR/MNAR imputation

Replicate-based imputation is designed for MAR values. When a dataset contains both MAR and MNAR values, `impute_replicate_mixed_se()` can combine replicate-based imputation with an MNAR imputation method.

For example, `MinProb` can be used for MNAR values:

```{r mixed imputation}
set.seed(123)

imputed_se <- impute_replicate_mixed_se(
  example_se,
  p = 0.05,
  MNAR_method = "MinProb",
  MNAR_args = list(q = 0.01)
)
```

The workflow first performs replicate-based imputation for MAR values. MNAR values are then restored to their original missing state and passed to the selected MNAR imputation method.

If no MNAR imputation is desired, set MNAR method to `none`.

# Choosing the variability parameter

The `p` argument controls the fraction of observations with the highest standard deviations that are used to estimate the global standard deviation.

For example:

```{r standard deviation parameter}
set.seed(123)

imputed_se <- impute_replicate_se(
  example_se,
  p = 0.05
)
```

uses the top 5% of standard deviations to calculate the median global standard deviation.
